source.credit: Rendered by Ansatz from a law drawn by drand round 6604796 and sealed (SHA-256 committed and pushed) before the run

subjects.description: small orange rectangular block attached to the bottom of a vertical spring

observation.what_happens: An orange block hanging from a vertical spring oscillates up and down in the centre of the frame. The motion is already underway at the start and continues oscillating up and down through the end of the clip.

calibration.note: no scale: lengths are in pixels

reasoning: The s channel shows large ~150 px near-sinusoidal up-down motion with period ~1.05 s and near-constant amplitude, x is noise. This is a vertical mass-spring oscillator. Candidates go from ideal SHM to linear viscous damping to added quadratic air drag to cubic stiffness to test loss and nonlinearity on the held-back segment.

caveats: Misses are still many times the measurement noise
Friction and swing-coupling knobs are unconstrained with one at its limit
Choice rests on held-out frames not shown here
Plain damped and Duffing springs miss by far more
critique.finding: The block bounces like a spring with bounce rate {omega} around rest spot {seq} plus a sideways wobble {omega_s} tweaking it. It only partly captures the motion, leaving a growing wiggle in its misses.
critique.headline: Springy block bounces on, model partly keeps up
critique.why_it_won: It lets sideways swing nudge the stiffness while adding dry rubbing, so it stays near the bounces while plain damped or Duffing laws swing far off.

preRevision.revision_idea: Add dry coil friction plus a slight sideways swing that modulates effective length. The misses keep the bounce rhythm with waxing and waning size that viscous damping alone cannot shape.

headline: A law drawn by public randomness, sealed before the run: a linear spring with quadratic damping and a drive. Missed: no model proposed the drive; the miss is published.
finding: The block bounces like a spring with bounce rate about 13 rad/s around rest spot about 87 px plus a sideways wobble about 19 rad/s tweaking it. It only partly captures the motion, leaving a growing wiggle in its misses.

eyeball.confidence: low - rough visual estimate from few stills, ~7 s clip, assumed ~1 Hz oscillation with light damping
eyeball.law_in_words: vertical damped harmonic motion about gravity-shifted equilibrium: x'' + gamma x' + omega^2 (x - seq) = 0, with omega = sqrt(k/m)

truth.note: This clip was rendered from a law drawn by public randomness (drand round 6604796) and sealed before the run: its SHA-256 was committed and pushed in 2752b74, the law revealed in b66261e. Missed. The drawn law was a linear spring with quadratic damping and a periodic drive; Ansatz's winner was a spring with dry friction whose stiffness is modulated by a hidden second oscillator. No drive term was proposed by Muse Spark, the referee or Muse Wonder. The only constant the two laws share is the natural frequency, 5% high. With no ruler found, lengths are in pixels; true values in pixels use the render's own scale.

drawn.equation: x'' = -(k/m) x - cq x'|x'| + F0 cos(wd t)
drawn.x: displacement below the resting point (m, down positive); t from release

F0.rule: F0 / |w0^2 - wd^2| = share of A uniform in [0.15, 0.35] (drawn 0.225)

wd.rule: wd / w0 uniform in [0.55, 0.8] or [1.25, 1.6], each half the time (drawn 0.566)
